Most neuroscientists think your mind is just your brain. So why do most still believe in free will?
In a PNAS survey of 2,657 of them, sixty-four percent said every thought comes down to the working brain.
Yet only seventeen point five percent said our nervous system leaves us no freedom.
One explanation: two levels. Zoom in, and neurons follow causes. Zoom out, and a person weighs options and chooses.
Only one in seventy-two invited researchers replied: a snapshot, not a verdict.
Still, the idea that neuroscience killed free will was not the majority view.
